core_obligations: Choose representatives (proof lines 9097-9099): take a K-flat complex K^bullet representing K and an arbitrary complex L^bullet representing L.

Resolve tensored objects injectively (proof lines 9099-9102): choose a K-injective complex J^bullet and a quasi-isomorphism Tot(K^bullet tensor L^bullet) -> J^bullet, so that SheafHom^bullet(L^bullet, J^bullet) represents RSheafHom(L, K tensor^L L).

Build the composite (proof lines 9102-9110): take the first arrow K^bullet -> SheafHom^bullet(L^bullet, Tot(K^bullet tensor L^bullet)) from the cited diagonal lemma, and follow it by the arrow induced by the quasi-isomorphism into J^bullet; this composite is the asserted canonical morphism.
proof_roadmap: Represent K by a K-flat complex and L arbitrarily.
Resolve the total tensor product by a K-injective complex J.
Take the diagonal map from the earlier same-chapter lemma and post-compose with the map induced by the quasi-isomorphism.
The target then represents RSheafHom(L, K tensor^L L), which gives the statement.
difficulty_reason: The lemma constructs the canonical morphism K -> RSheafHom(L, K tensor^L L) on the derived category of a ringed site (statement lines 9086-9094). The construction again hinges on resolution choices: K must be represented by a K-flat complex so that the total tensor product represents K tensor^L L, and that total tensor product must be replaced by a K-injective J^bullet so that the internal hom into it computes the derived internal hom (proof lines 9097-9102). With those choices the morphism is the composite of the diagonal map and the map induced by the quasi-isomorphism (proof lines 9102-9110). The claim is H2: one construction whose content is the recognition of the two represented objects, exactly as in the companion lemmas of the same section.
